title: Permission handoff orchestration: staged shadowing, synthetic canaries, audit-forwarding and SSO mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a runbook to move permissions and admin controls from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 using a conservative, telemetry-driven approach. Goals: preserve auditability, maintain customer-admin UX, avoid permission regressions, and provide fast rollback/fallback paths.

Scope:
- Dual-write shim for live reads/writes while backfills run
- Deterministic backfill jobs with idempotency and reconciliation
- Synthetic canaries exercising admin flows (create role, assign, escalate, revoke)
- SSO/SAML attribute harmonization and mapping verification
- Audit-forwarding so v2 events are preserved in long-term audit store before v1 deprecation
- Cutover gating and customer opt-in communications

High-level approach:
1) Dual-write proxy: implement a lightweight proxy that writes permission changes to both v1 and v2 stores for specified org waves. Reads default to v1 until canary validation passes.
2) Incremental backfills: schedule per-org background jobs that compute deltas, run in small batches, and emit reconciliation events into a validation queue. Each backfill run produces a checksum and row-count metrics.
3) Synthetic canaries: run headless integration tests against canary orgs that mirror customer-critical admin flows, execute hourly during canary window, and surface diffs to telemetry dashboards.
4) SSO/SAML mapping verification: validate attribute transforms for NameID, groups, and role-claim translations; run mapping dry-runs and flag ambiguous mappings for manual review.
5) Audit-forwarding: stream RBAC v2 decision and change events to the existing audit pipeline (and into cold storage) so historical trails remain continuous. Ensure event schema compatibility and secure signing.
6) Cutover plan: wave-based opt-in model with a go/no-go gating step driven by canary health, reconciliation success rate (>99.8%), and audit-forwarding completeness.
7) Rollback: dual-write continues for a fixed interval post-cutover. If regressions appear, flip reads back to v1 and pause further waves; issue incident runbook.

Key trade-offs and decisions made so far:
- Dual-write vs big-bang backfill: chose dual-write to reduce blast radius and provide fast rollback. This increases complexity in reconciliation and latency on writes for canary orgs.
- Reconciliation frequency: hourly delta runs chosen to balance load vs time-to-detect drift.
- Audit-forward before cutover: must be enabled early to avoid gaps in forensic trails; we prioritized streaming over bulk exports.
- Mapping ambiguity handling: ambiguous SAML group-to-role mappings are surfaced to a manual review queue instead of automatic assignment. This reduces risk for enterprise customers.

Runbook: (engineer steps)
- Preflight (2 weeks before wave): run schema validation, enable audit-forwarding in staging, run synthetic canaries in staging orgs, sign off mapping spreadsheets with SEs.
- Canary wave (week 0): pick 5 internal/test orgs + 2 opt-in customers; enable dual-write and backfill; run synthetic canaries continuously for 72h.
- Validation (during canary): monitor reconciliation success rate, canary end-to-end latencies, and audit ingestion lag. Required metrics: reconciliation_pass_rate >= 99.8%, canary_e2e_p95 < 350ms, audit_forward_lag < 2 min.
- Expand waves: if canary stable, expand to 50 orgs in week 1, then 500 in week 2, opening to full rollout after wave 4.
- Post-cutover: keep dual-write for 30 days for roaming fixes, then run final full sweep and decommission v1 write path.

Safety and observability:
- Telemetry dashboards: permission-diff-rate, reconciliation_pass_rate, canary_e2e_p50/p95/p99, audit_forward_lag, sso_mapping_error_rate.
- Alerts: reconciliation_pass_rate < 99.5% for 30m => P0 page; audit_forward_lag > 5m for 10m => P0; sso_mapping_error_rate spike => SE triage.
- Forensics: signed event IDs and checksum stored with each backfill run; make these searchable in audit explorer.

Customer communications (template summary):
- Pre-cutover notice: describe opt-in canaries, expected impact (none for most), timeline, and rollback guarantees.
- Wave invites: allow customers to opt into earlier waves via Consent form; provide SE assistance for SSO mapping.
- Post-cutover confirmation: include link to audit export and contact for discrepancies.

Open risks and mitigation:
- SAML attribute collisions: mitigated by manual review queue and deny-listing auto-mapping for groups with ambiguous labels.
- Backfill scale: run rate-limited workers and prioritise high-traffic orgs; fallback to incremental per-resource backfills if DB pressure high.
- Audit forwarding schema mismatch: maintain translation layer with versioned envelope and fallbacks to raw payload.

Artifacts and references:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RBAC/RBACv2+handoff+design
- SAML mapping spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1SamlMappingHandoff
- Draft customer comms (Google Doc): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RBAC-Comm-Draft
- Canary scripts repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-canaries/tree/eng/dualwrite
- Reconciliation job PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8124

Acceptance criteria:
- All canary orgs show reconciliation_pass_rate >= 99.8% for 72h and no production incidents for admin flows.
- SSO mapping errors reduced to zero in canary orgs or moved to manual queue with owner.
- Audit-forwarding shows continuous event stream with <2min median lag and no dropped envelopes.
- Customer opt-in UI and comms templates published and legal-approved.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Finish dual-write proxy telemetry (ENG-998200) and finalize reconciliation metrics.
- Legal and Security sign-off on audit-forwarding schema.
- Schedule first canary wave and add SE contacts for opted-in customers.
